Our expectation for mods is that by default (a) they are non-commercial in nature, (b) are based on the official SDK for one of our games and (c) clearly communicate their status as a community project. Non-commercial By "non-commercial," we mean that anyone who owns the original Valve game can download and play the mod for free. Your mod should not be used to support a commercial endeavor. If your mod includes paid advertising or requires payment, whether in the game itself or outside of it, it is considered commercial. If a player can receive items, features, or gameplay after making a payment of any kind or a “donation,” it is considered a commercial use. Based on the Official SDK We provide SDKs for many of our games, and these are the approved tools for modding. It’s important to note that shipping a mod based on leaked or stolen source code is not permitted. Clear Communication Your mod should have a distinct identity, and should not suggest that it was created or endorsed by Valve. This extends to all places where you talk about your mod, including its title. We may deny titles that imply a mod being an official prequel, sequel or remake of a Valve title. Bad titles: Ricochet 2 Ricochet Classic Ricochet: Source Better titles: Deflection – A Ricochet Mod Collider – A Ricochet Story As long as you follow these guidelines, you can freely distribute your mod through Steam, your own website, or any third-party service without needing a separate license from Valve. Frequently Asked Questions Q. I wish to distribute a Source Engine Mod through Steam. Should I fill out the paperwork? A. Yes, please complete the regular digital paperwork to get signed up as a Steamworks developer. All information is required, including bank and tax information and app fee even if you intend to distribute your mod for free. Q. Is there a licensing fee for using the Source Engine? A. There are no fees for using the Source Engine for your free mod. Q. I’ve got a Source mod that I want to distribute via Steam. How do I prepare my mod under my app ID? A. You'll need to copy the exe and content from the Valve Source Engine game you have built your mod off of and wrap that up as your application.
